text:
tara: heads-up — ran into a confusing mypy/pyright failure in the onboarding sampleapp when combining autogenerated pydantic models, AsyncClient, and our token refresher auth wrapper. affects new users who pip install the SDK and follow the quickstart.

ben: ugh that’s painful. minimal repro?

tara: yeah, super small:
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient, models
client = AsyncClient(api_key=os.environ['API_KEY'], auth=TokenRefreshAuth(...), retry=RetryConfig(max_attempts=1))
async def main():
    async for ev in client.chat.stream('hey'):
        print(ev.author.id)
```
pyright: Type of "client.chat.stream" is "Any"
mypy: error: "Coroutine" not subscriptable at the `async for` line

yuki: is this on a clean venv with the published wheel or a local editable install? sometimes stubs are missing from editable installs.

tara: this is with the published wheel (0.9.2). I inspected the installed .pyi and the stream method return is unparametrized: `-> AsyncIterator` (no [models.ChatEvent]) and there are several missing imports like Annotated/AsyncIterator in the top of the pyi.

ben: could be two issues colliding: 1) our stubgen fails to materialize forward refs when annotations future is present, and 2) when init kwargs include protocols like TokenRefreshAuth the overload resolution in the pyi generation falls back to Any for the client instance.

yuki: we added a smoke test for mypy before, but maybe it didn't cover sampeapps that pass both auth+retry together. raising an issue is good.

tara: filed https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/issues/1055 with repro and attached the installed pyi. PR idea: ensure renderer emits explicit typing imports (AsyncIterator, Union, Annotated, Literal) whenever generics or Annotated are used, and prefer emitting AsyncIterator[ConcreteEvent] instead of bare AsyncIterator. also add a packaging test to ensure .pyi files are bundled in the wheel (PEP 561).

ben: quick workaround for onboarding docs: show an explicit typed example users can copy-paste: add `from typing import AsyncIterator` and annotate the iterator before the loop, or cast it. eg:
```py
from typing import AsyncIterator, cast
it = cast(AsyncIterator[models.ChatEvent], client.chat.stream('hey'))
async for ev in it:
    ...
```

yuki: doc change + issue/PR sounds great. I'll take the patch to the pyi renderer and the packaging check. can someone add a sampleapp integration test that runs mypy/pyright against the example? that would catch regressions.

doc-bot: CI: packaging-smoke failed on PR 4761 — missing .pyi in wheel for py3.9 build: https://ci.redwood.dev/4761/5

tara: thanks. assigning follow-ups: yuki -> pyi renderer + tests, ben -> sampleapp mypy/pyright smoke, tara -> update onboarding docs with workaround and link to issue.

ben: one more note — recommend we avoid returning plain Union[Client, AsyncClient] from helpers used in samples. better to provide explicit overloads (@overload with Literal[True]/Literal[False]) so typecheckers can narrow. that approach reduced confusion in a previous bug.

yuki: agreed. i'll also add a unit that inspects generated stubs for bare generics and fails CI if any are present.

tara: great — saved a new hire some time. thanks team :coffee:
